title: Speak Ads Strategy: Locales, Onboard Paywalls & App Store | Sprites
summary: How Speak runs Meta ads through App Store installs, start.speak.com paywall quizzes, Korea sales events and 220 LinkedIn B2B ads — with almost no creator partners.
body_markdown:
Speak is the AI language tutor that wants you talking out loud. French ads say it is 3.7× more effective. Korean ads scream a flash sale. Spanish ads put an AI tutor on the hook. And more than half of the Meta ads I read never open a website at all — they dump you into the App Store.


I pulled 560 Meta ads from their library, measured the top video files, resolved the start.speak.com onboard shells, walked the Korea and France landings, and read the 220 LinkedIn ads beside them.


Same split as Viktor, Clay, Wispr Flow and Suno: the Creative Factory, then the Performance Machine.


## Speak ads: key findings


- **560** Meta ads in the library (all with end dates in this snapshot)
- **445** video (79%), **62** static, **53** carousel
- **294** unique video files; top clones run 3–6 ad objects each
- Funnel: **App Store 237** , **start.speak.com 113** , **www.speak.com 112** , **Play Store 58** , **HubSpot 20**
- ` start.speak.com` injects an **onboard config** with` redirectType: "paywall"`
- Median short video ~ **22 seconds** ; a few long-form testimonials run past **3 minutes**
- **9:16** dominates (352 of the sized videos)
- Partners: only **7** partnership ads across **4** names — almost none
- LinkedIn: **220** ads, Asia B2B (JP / TW / CN HR outreach), not recruiting
- Korea runs sales events + gated HR prompt packs on HubSpot with real UTM campaign names


Top Speak video files sampled around 1.2 seconds. Collected 23 September 2026.


## Part 1: The Creative Factory


### One product, many languages


Format Ads Share


Video 445 79%


Static 62 11%


Carousel 53 9%


Behind the video ads sit 294 unique files. Nothing clones like Suno's Studio unlock (29 objects). Speak spreads volume across many short cuts: the most-cloned files here sit at six and five objects.


The creative splits by market, not by format:


- **English:** "Talk Out Loud. Get Feedback." and "Speak Spanish with your AI tutor."
- **French:** "Un coach virtuel d'anglais", "Parlez en 7 jours", "3,7 plus efficace"
- **Polish / Italian:** the same 3.7× efficacy claim, localized
- **Korean:** sale banners, celebrity (Kim Woo-bin), New Year resolutions


**The hook is the language of the market.** The ask is almost always install or start a trial.


### Hold the take. Grade the mouth.


Of the 17 short videos I measured under 90 seconds:


- Median length about **22 seconds** . A separate long-form lane runs 198–212 seconds.
- **9:16** is the default. Squares show up on some web shells.
- Median cuts in the first six seconds: **1** . Some French and Spanish cuts jump harder (7–17).


Wispr cuts once and titles like TikTok. Suno holds a home studio for six seconds because the audio is the ad. Speak holds a face mid-sentence and drops a feedback card — the product is the correction.


A language app can afford to not cut. The mouth is the creative.

### Learn More is the soft ask


437 ads have no CTA string. Learn More is 69. See Details 31. Install Now only 19 — even though hundreds of destinations are store URLs. Meta's CTA field and the destination disagree often; the path is the real ask.


Headline tests recycle the same proof structures: efficacy multiplier, days-to-speak, celebrity, sale urgency. The variable is the language. The door stays install or onboard.


## Part 2: The Performance Machine


Now the half you cannot see in the feed.


### Four doors, one product


Door Ads What it is


App Store` id1286609883` 237 Default consumer install. Biggest path in the library.


` start.speak.com/*` 113 Onboard quiz shells that redirect to a paywall.


` www.speak.com` locales 112 US try, France BAU, Korea event pages.


Play Store 58 Android twin of the App Store door.


HubSpot forms 20 Korea B2B MQLs with filled UTM campaign names.


Wispr hides campaign names behind short links you can resolve. Suno leaves Warp macros unfilled but shows the Statsig door. Speak does both store installs and a web onboard — and on HubSpot, the UTMs actually resolve.


**How you get this without an ads manager login.** The Meta Ad Library returns the destination string. Store URLs are the strategy for half the account. For web, fetch` start.speak.com/{slug}` and read` window.__ONBOARD_CONFIG__` — that JSON is the funnel.


### start.speak.com is a paywall machine


Fetch` start.speak.com/speakcom-c0180` (or` ce055` ,` cfb78` ,` c9d85` ) and you do not get a marketing page. You get a client shell that embeds:


Field What it does


` flowSlug` Which onboard flow this ad bought — e.g.` speakcom-c0180`


` redirectType` Always` paywall` in the shells I opened


` steps` 8–9 step indices: quiz → intent → paywall


` theme.primaryColor`` #1c49ff` Speak blue across flows


` language` /` country` Locale baked into the config, not just the URL


start.speak.com — Segment analytics, noindex, paywall redirect. The ad never has to change when the quiz does.


Same job Suno gives Statsig and Wispr gives Dub: keep the ad, swap the experience. Speak's version is an onboard flow ID in the path.


### www.speak.com is the brand and the promo


The brand door. Most paid traffic skips it for the store or start.speak.com. /us/try — Statsig + Amplitude + Segment + Webflow. Trial-forward. /fr/bau — Back to school. Calendar creative for a locale.


Korea's event URLs (` /ko/event/26sep-d100/home` , early-bird, December brand) were the live promo doors in the library; some had already 404'd by the time I re-fetched them. The ads still point at the sale. The calendar is the campaign name.


### Seven days free. Then Premium.


Speak does not publish a stable public pricing grid the way Suno does. The App Store listing is the source of truth in this teardown:


Plan Monthly Annual Notes


Trial — — 7 days full access, then charge


Premium ~$18 ~$84 Core tutor, roleplay, Ask Speak Tutor


Premium Plus ~$40 ~$165 Unlimited custom lessons + study plan


There is no durable free tier. The ad promises a trial; the store collects the card. That is why Install Now and the App Store path matter more than a marketing-site pricing table.


Gate What it costs you What it gets them


7-day trial A card on file Habit before the charge


Store listing An install Skips the website entirely


Onboard paywall Quiz answers + trial Intent data before payment


Premium Plus ~$2× Premium Power-user upsell

### Korea is consumer sales and B2B MQLs


Twenty HubSpot form ads share filled UTMs. Example campaign names from the library:


- ` APAC_KR_GatedContent_Downloaded_MQL_HRPrompt`
- ` APAC_KR_Audrey_MQL_Trial`


Medium is` image` or` carousel` . Content is` HRprompt` . This is the opposite of Suno's unfilled Warp macros — Speak's Korea B2B lane writes the campaign name into the URL on purpose.


### LinkedIn is the enterprise twin


220 LinkedIn ads. Not recruiting. Not product install. Asia B2B outbound: Japanese survey-for-report offers, Taiwan and China HR sequences from "Jamie" at Speak, training-budget objections, Starbucks-card incentives for form completes.


Meta is the consumer install channel. LinkedIn is the company training channel. Same product, different buyer.


### Almost no Meta partners


Only 7 of 560 Meta ads are paid partnerships — four named creators. Speak is not running a Suno-style musician roster on Meta. The celebrity weight sits in Korea brand films (Kim Woo-bin), not in a partner gallery of dozens.

Portraits are Instagram profile photos where the account is public. Speak's Meta partner volume is tiny next to Suno's 122 partnership ads.


## What actually makes this work


The Creative Factory is a localization desk. The same efficacy claim and talk-out-loud demo ship in French, Polish, Italian, Korean and Spanish — with sale and celebrity variants for Korea.


The Performance Machine is two doors. The App Store takes the install.` start.speak.com` takes the quiz and the paywall. HubSpot and LinkedIn take the company buyer in Asia.


Suno built a partner roster and a Statsig door. Speak built a language map and an onboard paywall.


Same job. Different machine.
